title: Optioner spec
description: A decision page: questions an AI agent asks a human. Text fields (context, prompt, description) accept Markdown.

optioner.$comment: Must be the integer 1. JSON Schema cannot tell 1 from 1.0, so 1.0 passes here while the Optioner validator rejects it; write it without a fraction or exponent.

context.$comment: Optional fields accept null as a synonym for "omitted", because generators that always emit every field cannot tell the two apart.

id.$comment: Ids must also be unique within a spec. JSON Schema cannot express that across array items, so the Optioner validator is stricter than this schema on that one rule.

allOf.$comment: A choice needs at least two real options, so the lower bound lives here rather than on the options keyword itself. "type": "array" is required as well: options is nullable in general, but a null here would slip past minItems and leave the choice empty.
free_text and yes_no have no options to choose from. Values that carry no meaning are tolerated (an empty array, false, null, since a null options also passes maxItems); any real value is an error.

links.$comment: Third known divergence from the Optioner validator, after the 1.0 version literal and id uniqueness: a null *inside* the array ("links": [null]) is rejected here but accepted by the validator, which decodes it to an empty string and renders an empty link. Safe direction — this schema is the stricter side, so anything it accepts also loads; writing the schema loosely enough to match would mean promising that [null] renders, which it does not.
